title: Kill 60 percent of mutants in inflection
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 286 mutants in the installed inflection/__init__.py of inflection==0.5.1, a regex-rule-driven English inflection library (pluralize, singularize, camelize, underscore, ordinalize and friends). Author a pytest suite from scratch under work/gc-349/tests/ that kills at least 60 percent of those mutants using only the stdlib, pytest==8.2.2, and the target package. The rule tables make many mutants subtle: plan a word list per rule family, grade, inspect survivors by mutant ID, add targeted words that distinguish each mutated rule, and re-grade until the threshold holds. The grader is fail-closed: red baseline, a suite slower than 6 seconds, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift scores kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi inflection==0.5.1 (target under mutation; single-module string-inflection library)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-349/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-349/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-349/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-349/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-349/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
An honest per-iteration log of wall-clock and LLM spend exists at work/gc-349/cost_log.md, including failed iterations.
